answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce token deposit before joining a market, then slash that deposit when a verified dispute proves fraud. One person can still create many identities, but each identity must tie up capital and risk losing it; spreading a fixed budget across sybils makes each less useful and raises the cost of attack. A prism of reputation signals may guide review, while a thread of signed actions links claims over time; even a comet of fresh accounts must post collateral.
